title: Even the birds in flight know how to praise Him.
subtitle: Every creature has its own prayer

row.title: its own prayer
sub: the way it was guided to

then: Ibn Kathir explains that angels, humans, jinn, animals and even inanimate things glorify Allah. The birds glorify Him {idea}while they are flying,{/idea} each with the way it was inspired and guided to. He compares it to the verse that the seven heavens and earth glorify Him.
now: You are stuck in traffic, scrolling. Above the windscreen a flock of birds turns in the sky. They are not wasting the moment. {idea}They are in prayer, in their own way.{/idea} You are the one creature who can choose whether to join.
old: Nature is just scenery while I get on with life.
new: Everything around me is already praising Allah; I am invited to join.
try: The next time you see birds flying, say SubhanAllah once with them.

title: Everything belongs to Him, and everything returns to Him.
subtitle: The owner and the destination are the same
then: After showing all creation praising Allah, the verse names Him the owner of all. Ibn Kathir explains He is {idea}the Ruler and Controller,{/idea} and the return to Him is on the Day of Resurrection, when He will judge. He closes with {reward}to Him be praise at the beginning and in the end.{/reward}
now: The mortgage papers say it is yours. The payslip says the salary is yours. The verse reads both documents and adds a line: {idea}borrowed, and returning.{/idea} It is not a threat. It is relief. You are not holding the whole world up. He is.
old: I need to control everything I own.
new: Everything belongs to Allah and returns to Him, including me.
try: Look at one thing you worry about owning or losing. Say: it belongs to Allah, and to Him it returns.

title: Watch a storm form and see Whose hand is in it.
subtitle: Clouds driven, joined, piled, and opened
then: Ibn Kathir describes Allah driving the clouds from when they are {idea}still weak,{/idea} then joining and piling them, and rain coming from the gaps. Ubayd bin Umayr spoke of winds that stir, form, join and seed the clouds. The rain and hail may be {reward}mercy for some{/reward} and held back from others.
now: The weather app shows a storm coming. You check it to see if your commute will be wet. Next time, step outside and watch it build. {idea}Every step was driven.{/idea} The flash that makes you squint is a reminder of how small your eyes are next to His power.
old: Weather is just the climate doing its thing.
new: Every cloud is driven, joined, and opened by Allah, as mercy or as warning.
try: The next time it rains, step to a window and make a dua while it falls.

title: Night and day trade places, and it is a lesson.
subtitle: Something lengthens, something shortens, by His command
then: Ibn Kathir explains Allah {idea}takes from the length of one and adds to the other{/idea} until they are equal, then reverses it. He controls this by His command, power and knowledge. He links it to the verse that the alternation of night and day holds {reward}signs for people of understanding.{/reward}
now: Your alarm goes off in the dark in winter. In summer it is already light. You complain both times. The verse asks you to {idea}look up from the complaint.{/idea} The same hand that shifts the seasons shifts the hard and easy seasons of your life.
new: Every turning of night into day is a sign for those who look.
try: Watch the sunset or sunrise once this week without your phone, and just notice it.

title: One water, and a world of creatures from it.
subtitle: Bellies, two legs, four legs, as He wills

row.title: He creates what He wills
sub: He is able to do all

then: Ibn Kathir notes Allah mentions His power to create all kinds of animals, {idea}with their different forms, colors and ways of moving,{/idea} from one kind of water. What He wills happens, and {reward}He is able to do all things.{/reward}
now: Your toddler is fascinated by an ant on the pavement. A dog walks past. A pigeon lands. You are rushing to the car. The verse slows you down: {idea}all of it came from water,{/idea} each made differently on purpose. Your child is seeing something true.
old: Animals are just background to my day.
new: Every creature, so different, is a sign of the One who creates what He wills.
try: Stop for one minute today and really look at an animal. Notice how it moves.

title: The verses are clear. Guidance is His to give.
subtitle: A short line between the signs and the hypocrites
then: After the signs of clouds, night and day and animals, the verse sums up. Ibn Kathir explains Allah has sent {idea}clear rulings, words of wisdom and parables,{/idea} and guides people of understanding to {reward}ponder and understand them.{/reward}
now: You have watched a dozen videos on faith and still feel unsure. It is not more information you need. {idea}The verses are already clear.{/idea} What you ask for is guidance itself, and that is asked of Allah, not of the algorithm.
old: I need one more proof before I commit.
new: The signs are clear; guidance is a gift I ask Allah for.
try: In your next prayer, say Ihdina as-sirat al-mustaqim slowly and mean it as a request.

title: We believe and we obey, said the ones who turned away.
subtitle: When the words and the actions part ways
then: Ibn Kathir describes the hypocrites of Madinah, {trap}who show one thing while hiding another.{/trap} They said they believed and obeyed, then turned away. Their actions contradicted their words: {trap}they say what they do not do.{/trap}
now: You say yes in the family meeting, then quietly do the opposite. You agree in the team call, then never follow through. Small versions of this live in all of us. The verse is a mirror, {idea}not a label for someone else.{/idea}
old: I said the right thing, so I am on the right side.
new: Faith is proven when my actions keep the promise my words made.
try: Find one promise you made to Allah or to someone and did not keep. Keep it today.

title: Called to judgment, they turned aside.
subtitle: Refusing the standard when it might go against you
then: Ibn Kathir explains that when the hypocrites were asked to follow the guidance revealed to the Messenger ﷺ, {trap}they turned away, too proud of themselves.{/trap} He compares it to the verses about those who claim belief but turn away from the Prophet ﷺ with aversion.
now: A family inheritance. A business split. You know what is fair according to your faith. You also know a cleverer route that gives you more. {trap}The moment you look away from the standard{/trap} is the moment this verse describes. It is a test of the heart, not of the lawyer.
old: I will follow the guidance when it is convenient.
new: Turning from Allah's standard when it costs me shows what my heart really holds.
try: Think of one disagreement you are in. Ask honestly: what would be fair before Allah?

title: When the ruling suited them, they came running.
subtitle: Obedience that depends on winning
then: Ibn Kathir explains that if the judgment was going to be in their favor, they came and listened and obeyed. But {trap}their acceptance was not because it was the truth,{/trap} only because it matched their desires. When the truth went against them, {trap}they turned away from it.{/trap}
now: You quote the hadith about rights of the husband, or the wife, or the parents, when it helps your side. The ones that ask something of you, you skip. Everyone does it a little. The verse asks: {idea}do I follow the truth, or does the truth follow me?{/idea}
old: I follow the religion when it backs me up.
new: Following the truth only when it favors me is following my desire.
try: Find one teaching you tend to quote against others. Apply it to yourself today.

title: Disease, doubt, or fear of unfairness? None of these.
subtitle: Three questions about a turning heart
then: Ibn Kathir explains the verse's questions: either their hearts had a disease, or they doubted the religion, or they feared Allah and His Messenger ﷺ would wrong them. Allah answers: {trap}it is they who are the wrongdoers.{/trap} Allah and His Messenger ﷺ {idea}are free of the unfairness they imagine.{/idea}
now: When you resist something Allah asks, notice the story you tell yourself. "It is unfair to me." "It does not fit modern life." "Maybe it is not really from Allah." The verse invites you to check {idea}the heart that is telling the story.{/idea}
old: When I resist a teaching, the teaching must be the problem.
new: Resistance to what Allah asks often comes from a disease, doubt, or fear in me.
try: Ask Allah tonight to heal your heart from any doubt or disease it is carrying.
